# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 27 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 36 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_027_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 27

**1** "If you do not fast with respect to the world, you will not find the kingdom.

**2** If you do not observe the Sabbath as a Sabbath, you will not see the Father."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"Fast with respect to the world"** — LOGOS preferred over PNEUMA's "fast from the world." The Coptic uses a relational construction (*ebol ha*); "with respect to" is more precise than the directional "from."

**"Observe the Sabbath as a Sabbath"** — LOGOS/EMET preferred over PNEUMA's "keep the Sabbath as a real Sabbath." The tautology ("Sabbath as a Sabbath") is in the Coptic and is deliberate — the point is to do the thing AS the thing, not a substitute.

**Tension with Sayings 6 and 14:** Saying 6 rejects fasting/prayer/almsgiving; Saying 14 repeats this. Saying 27 reinstates fasting and Sabbath. The resolution in Thomas scholarship: 27 refers to cosmological/ascetic practices (fasting from the world = world-renunciation; Sabbath = achieved rest) rather than the liturgical calendar observances rejected in 6 and 14.

**P.Oxy 1 parallel:** Lines 4-11 preserve the Greek: "If you do not abstain from the world, you will not find the kingdom of God." The Greek uses *nēsteuō* (fast/abstain).

**Synoptic Parallels:** No direct parallel. The "fasting from the world" concept has echoes in Paul (Rom 12:2; "do not be conformed to this world") and in the Johannine "not of the world" theme (John 17:16).
